scope: Ten unscored health, weather and discovery companions retained or updated for Edition 03. Original research snapshot September 8 at 19:00 PDT; the orbital-delivery item was updated at the new edition cutoff. No live alerts.

items.title: Hawaii: weakening wind does not remove flood danger
items.reported: NHC/CPHC describes Lowell weakening and moving northward. The NHC page still flags a flash-flooding threat in the Hawaiian Islands.
items.concern: Storm category alone does not describe rainfall, surf, damaged roads or recovery needs. This saved orb is not a current emergency-warning service.
items.possibleChange: Improving conditions could allow restoration work; lingering rainfall and damage could keep travel and services disrupted.
items.watchFor: Current Honolulu/NHC advisories and local emergency instructions. Use their current issue times, not this snapshot, for safety decisions.

items.title: US heat and storms: impacts follow different clocks
items.reported: WPC’s September 8 extended outlook describes lingering late-summer heat in the southern Plains. Its short-range discussion also identifies rainfall and thunderstorm risks elsewhere.
items.concern: Heat stress, electricity demand and flood disruption can matter before they become national headlines. Regional outlooks do not predict conditions at every address.
items.possibleChange: A change in the weather pattern could ease heat; overlapping hazards could strain local services.
items.watchFor: Updated local forecasts and warnings, observed impacts and restoration reports. The cited outlook’s dates are shorter than the full orb window.

items.title: Nepal: the recovery is part of the event
items.reported: AP describes severe damage to homes, roads, bridges and hydropower after Nepal’s August floods, testing its new government.
items.concern: The flood occurred before this forecast window. Rescue, displacement and infrastructure recovery can nevertheless change people’s lives during it.
items.possibleChange: Restored transport and electricity would mark improvement. Continuing access problems could slow relief and economic recovery.
items.watchFor: Verified rescue and recovery updates, reopened routes and functioning power infrastructure. Avoid treating preliminary loss estimates as final totals.

sources.title: AP · Nepal flood recovery and governance

items.title: Indonesia: reopening is a real positive signal
items.reported: AP reports that flights resumed at Jakarta-area and regional airports following volcanic ash closures.
items.concern: Reopening does not guarantee every flight will operate or that volcanic hazards have ended. Older closure reports can circulate after conditions change.
items.possibleChange: Stable operations could reduce disruption and help stranded travellers. New ash could force restrictions again.
items.watchFor: Current airport and airline notices, official volcanic advisories and actual flight operations. Do not invent a new eruption prediction.

sources.title: AP · flights resume after ash closures

items.title: DRC Ebola: a major concern with a precise classification
items.reported: WHO reports geographic expansion of the Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak. Its emergency committee report says the event remains a public health emergency of international concern, while not meeting the pandemic-emergency criteria.
items.concern: WHO identifies gaps in response coverage, access and community trust. An international emergency designation does not mean a pandemic is inevitable.
items.possibleChange: Stronger detection, care and community-led response could improve control; disrupted services could undermine it.
items.watchFor: New WHO and national updates with clear reporting periods. Separate reported cases, surveillance changes and evidence about transmission; do not project a fourteen-day case count from one headline.

items.title: Public health progress belongs in the picture too
items.reported: WHO has validated Bhutan’s elimination of dog-transmitted human rabies. This is a confirmed achievement before the orb window.
items.concern: Elimination of a defined public-health problem is not a claim that surveillance can stop or that all related risks everywhere have disappeared.
items.possibleChange: This is a constructive counterweight to crisis-only attention: sustained public-health work can produce measurable gains.
items.watchFor: Implementation and surveillance updates. Count the existing achievement as context, never as a prediction made after the fact.

items.title: AGI claims: the question that inspired the experiment
items.basis: Company release plus attributed public claim
items.reported: Axios reports that OpenAI’s Brockman believes Astra reaches AGI. OpenAI’s launch page describes new capabilities and evaluation results.
items.concern: A capability claim, a benchmark result and reliable prediction of open-world events are separate propositions. This small, selected, AI-assisted set cannot establish AGI or foreknowledge.
items.possibleChange: More capable tools could improve research and forecasting discipline. Whether they improve forecasts needs prospective comparison across many cases.
items.watchFor: Independent evaluations, repeatable tasks and all resolved forecasts, including misses. These eight calls are an exploratory case study, not a controlled AGI evaluation.

sources.title: OpenAI · Astra launch and evaluation conditions

items.title: Personal agents: the next change may be ordinary work
items.reported: Meta has announced Muse, a personal agent designed to take actions across services. Its safety paper describes boundaries on those actions.
items.concern: Delegated access brings questions about consent, privacy, mistaken actions and malicious instructions. Described safeguards are not proof that failures cannot occur.
items.possibleChange: Successful deployment could change everyday scheduling and project work. Reliability problems or restricted access could slow adoption.
items.watchFor: What users can actually access, reproducible completed tasks, documented failures and permission controls. Distinguish a launch demonstration from dependable use.

items.title: Apple: a confirmed event, an unconfirmed product story
items.reported: Apple’s developer newsletter confirms a special event on September 9. The calendar alone does not confirm any rumoured hardware, price or shipping date.
items.concern: A compelling rumour can quietly turn into an assumed fact. Announcement, preorder and delivery are three distinct milestones.
items.possibleChange: A new product or software capability could change consumer choices; a narrower launch could disappoint expectations.
items.watchFor: Apple’s actual announcements, regional availability and shipping terms. Record what is delivered by September 22 separately from what is merely promised.

items.title: Orbital deliveries: a grounded UAP wink
items.reported: NASA’s current Progress 96 event page marks the timing under review. An earlier release describes the planned supply delivery to the ISS.
items.concern: Earlier dates must not be presented as confirmed after the schedule changes.
items.possibleChange: A completed delivery would support life and research aboard the station. Our UAP motif is playful design, not a claim of unidentified technology.
items.watchFor: The revised timetable and an actual docking confirmation.

coverageNotes: This edition focuses its companion readings on health, weather and discovery. It does not claim an exhaustive global news scan.
World Watch contains context and possible changes, not extra scored outcomes.
Use current official warnings for real-world safety decisions.
